healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Public healthcare is basic and under-resourced. Private hospitals exist in Belize City and major towns. English is the official language. For serious conditions, evacuation to Mexico or the US is common.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is basic throughout Belize. The Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital in Belize City is the main referral hospital. Private clinics offer better service but are still limited. Rural and island areas (Ambergris Caye, Caye Caulker) have minimal facilities. Serious cases require evacuation to Merida or Cancun (Mexico) or the US.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in towns open 8am-6pm Monday-Saturday. Limited hours on Sundays. Very limited pharmacy access on islands and in rural areas.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are reasonably stocked in Belize City and major towns. English-speaking pharmacists. Many medications available without prescription. Prices are higher than neighboring countries. Bring essential medications, especially if visiting islands or rural areas.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is relaxed. Many medications including antibiotics available over the counter. Pharmacists can recommend treatments for common ailments.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Decriminalized in small amounts (up to 10 grams) but not legal. Do not bring cannabis products into the country.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription for opioid-based medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Pseudoephedrine products
restrictedMeds.note: Restricted due to potential for illicit drug manufacturing. Carry documentation.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications. English documentation is accepted. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring sufficient supplies, especially for island destinations.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential. Ensure coverage includes water sports, diving, and adventure activities. Evacuation to Mexico or the US may be needed for serious conditions. Diving insurance (DAN) recommended for scuba divers.

required: Yellow Fever (required if arriving from an endemic country)
recommended: Malaria prophylaxis (recommended for rural and western districts)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Malaria risk exists in rural areas, especially the western districts. Islands and Belize City are lower risk. Dengue fever is present — use insect repellent.

waterNotes: Tap water in Belize City and major towns is treated and generally safe, but bottled water is recommended for visitors. On islands and in rural areas, use bottled water. Water quality can vary after heavy rains.
foodSafetyTips: Food is generally safe at established restaurants. Belizean cuisine features fresh seafood, rice and beans. Street food from busy vendors is usually fine. Be cautious with raw seafood (ceviche) from unfamiliar sources. Wash fruits before eating.
medicalTourismNote: Belize is not a medical tourism destination. Some travelers visit for affordable dental work in border towns.
metaDescription: Health guide for Belize: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital (KHMH)
hospitals.notes: Main public referral hospital. The best-equipped facility in the country. Emergency department available 24/7.

hospitals.name: Belize Medical Associates
hospitals.notes: Private hospital offering better facilities and shorter wait times. 24-hour emergency service.

hospitals.name: San Pedro Polyclinic
hospitals.notes: Small clinic on the main tourist island. Handles basic emergencies. Serious cases transferred to Belize City by air.

hospitals.name: San Ignacio Hospital
hospitals.notes: Public hospital serving the western tourism district. Basic facilities. Near Xunantunich and other Maya sites.

dentalCare.availability: Limited but available in Belize City and major towns. Some dentists in border towns cater to budget travelers.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic but affordable. English-speaking dentists. Quality varies widely. Some travelers combine trips with dental visits.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies on the islands, you may need to fly to Belize City. Ask your hotel or resort for a dentist recommendation on the mainland.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited availability. Some counselors in Belize City.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited in Belize. English-speaking counselors exist but are scarce. Telehealth from the US or UK is the best option for ongoing mental health support.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited. Many buildings lack wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: KHMH has basic wheelchair access. Smaller facilities may not.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Water taxis to islands are not wheelchair-accessible. Private transfers are the best option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Islands have sandy paths that are challenging for wheelchairs. Contact resorts in advance about accessibility. Some higher-end resorts may have accessible rooms.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at major hospitals in Belize City.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been fully lifted. Tourism-dependent Belize has streamlined all entry requirements.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics provide English-language receipts. Pay out of pocket and submit for reimbursement. KHMH can provide documentation for insurance claims. Keep all receipts. Emergency evacuation costs should be covered by your insurer directly.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Belize Dollar is pegged to USD at 2:1. Most facilities accept USD. Island medical care may cost more.

medicalEvacuation.note: Air evacuation from islands to mainland is done by local air services. International evacuation to Mexico or the US is needed for serious trauma, cardiac events, or complex surgeries.
